guide.title: Itraconazole
guide.description: An antifungal investigated for cancer growth pathways, blood-vessel formation and treatment resistance.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Itraconazole is an antifungal with several distinct cancer research programs. The clinical evidence includes small exploratory trials and uncontrolled chemotherapy series; other cancer findings remain preclinical.

sentences.text: Itraconazole is an antifungal with several distinct cancer research programs.
The clinical evidence includes small exploratory trials and uncontrolled chemotherapy series; other cancer findings remain preclinical.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: Small studies found signals of activity in basal cell, prostate and lung cancers, but designs and endpoints differ. Ovarian and pancreatic reports combined itraconazole with chemotherapy, while colorectal, melanoma, AML and myeloma work cited here tested laboratory or animal models.

questions.question: What happened in ovarian cancer?
questions.answer: A retrospective report described nine patients with recurrent or persistent ovarian clear cell carcinoma treated with combination chemotherapy and itraconazole; it cannot isolate the antifungal’s contribution.

sentences.text: A retrospective report described nine patients with recurrent or persistent ovarian clear cell carcinoma treated with combination chemotherapy and itraconazole; it cannot isolate the antifungal’s contribution.

questions.question: What happened in advanced prostate cancer?
questions.answer: In a 46-man dose-comparison study, 48.0% in the high-dose group and 11.8% in the low-dose group were free of PSA progression at 24 weeks; there was no standard-care control.

sentences.text: In a 46-man dose-comparison study, 48.0% in the high-dose group and 11.8% in the low-dose group were free of PSA progression at 24 weeks; there was no standard-care control.

questions.question: What happened in lung cancer?
questions.answer: The 23-person trial found 67% versus 29% progression-free at three months (p=0.11); the small, prematurely closed study leaves substantial uncertainty.

sentences.text: The 23-person trial found 67% versus 29% progression-free at three months (p=0.11); the small, prematurely closed study leaves substantial uncertainty.

questions.question: Has colorectal benefit been shown in patients?
questions.answer: The cited result concerns cancer-cell dormancy and tumor growth in experimental models, not patient survival or symptoms.

sentences.text: The cited result concerns cancer-cell dormancy and tumor growth in experimental models, not patient survival or symptoms.

questions.question: What happened in pancreatic cancer?
questions.answer: The 38-patient retrospective series used itraconazole with docetaxel, gemcitabine and carboplatin; observed responses cannot be attributed to itraconazole alone.

sentences.text: The 38-patient retrospective series used itraconazole with docetaxel, gemcitabine and carboplatin; observed responses cannot be attributed to itraconazole alone.

questions.question: Has melanoma benefit been shown clinically?
questions.answer: The cited experiments demonstrated growth and signaling effects in melanoma models; they did not compare clinical outcomes in patients.

sentences.text: The cited experiments demonstrated growth and signaling effects in melanoma models; they did not compare clinical outcomes in patients.

questions.question: Did basal cell tumors shrink?
questions.answer: Among the treated patients, tumor area fell by 24% (95% CI 18.2% to 30.0%); this exploratory study was small and not a randomized efficacy comparison.

sentences.text: Among the treated patients, tumor area fell by 24% (95% CI 18.2% to 30.0%); this exploratory study was small and not a randomized efficacy comparison.

questions.question: Does antifungal use during AML prove an anti-leukemia effect?
questions.answer: No: prevention of fungal infection is a different purpose; the cited direct anti-leukemia finding comes from patient-derived cells and xenograft models.

sentences.text: No: prevention of fungal infection is a different purpose; the cited direct anti-leukemia finding comes from patient-derived cells and xenograft models.

questions.question: What has myeloma research shown?
questions.answer: Itraconazole with arsenic trioxide inhibited Hedgehog signaling in cells and mouse tumors; that experiment did not measure benefit in patients.

glossary.title: Hedgehog pathway
glossary.meaning: The Hedgehog pathway is a cell-signaling system that carries messages from the cell surface to the nucleus and helps regulate growth and development.
glossary.context: Hedgehog pathway inhibition means reduced activity of this cell-signaling system in a specified assay or tissue. A drug's established antifungal action does not prove that it inhibits Hedgehog signaling, and a biomarker change does not by itself establish a clinical cancer benefit.
glossary.examples: A Hedgehog inhibitor targets this signaling route. Whether a particular drug helps a particular cancer still requires clinical testing.

glossary.title: Hyphae
glossary.meaning: Hyphae are microscopic fungal filaments; a network of these filaments forms a mycelium.
glossary.context: Candida yeast-to-hypha morphogenesis is the transition from budding yeast to filamentous growth. Inhibiting new hyphal formation, killing existing filaments and clearing an infection in a patient are different outcomes.
glossary.examples: A change in fungal shape is a different observation from symptom resolution or clearance of infection in a patient.

originalAction.text: Itraconazole inhibits fungal ergosterol synthesis, impairing the fungal cell membrane. Its cancer-repurposing rationale involves several different actions: changing growth signals, restricting blood-vessel formation and disrupting mitochondrial energy metabolism. Hedgehog and WNT are signaling pathways involved in cell growth; angiogenesis is the formation of new blood vessels. The evidence ranges from experiments in cells and mice to pathway measurements in human tumors, so the biological explanation needs to be read alongside the model in which it was tested.

pathways.title: Hedgehog signaling and Smoothened
pathways.text: Hedgehog signaling can sustain the growth of some tumors. In cell experiments, itraconazole reduced pathway activity and prevented Smoothened from accumulating in the primary cilium, a signaling compartment on the cell surface. Pathway-mapping experiments placed its action near Smoothened, although this study did not directly establish a binding site. Fluconazole did not share the Hedgehog effect under the tested conditions.

pathways.title: Cholesterol transport and blood-vessel growth
pathways.text: In endothelial-cell experiments, itraconazole caused cholesterol transport inhibition. Cholesterol became trapped in endolysosomes while mTOR signaling and proliferation fell; supplying cholesterol to the cell membrane partly reversed these effects. Later binding and competition experiments identified the cholesterol-transport protein NPC1 as a target, alongside a separate VDAC1–AMPK pathway. These mechanisms help explain the anti-angiogenesis rationale, but do not establish cancer benefit in patients.

pathways.title: Human Hedgehog findings are mixed
pathways.text: Itraconazole has human treatment-response biomarker data, but those data do not establish consistent pathway inhibition. Gerber's lung-cancer window study enrolled 13 patients; 12 had paired skin biopsies, with no significant GLI1 or PTCH1 change. Antonarakis measured skin GLI1 changes and described the support for a tumor mechanism as indirect. A five-person study combined sequential arsenic trioxide and itraconazole, so its biomarker effect cannot be assigned to itraconazole alone; no tumor shrinkage was observed. Clinical inference is Low because these small exploratory studies use surrogate tissues or combination treatment and give conflicting pathway results.

pathways.title: An exploratory basal-cell carcinoma estimate remains unresolved
pathways.text: The exploratory basal-cell-carcinoma biomarker estimate remains unreconciled with its registry summaries. It should not be treated as a settled numerical estimate of pathway inhibition. This uncertainty is separate from the negative lung-cancer biomarker finding.

pathways.title: Fungal morphology is a separate mechanism question
pathways.text: In laboratory yeast isolates, itraconazole and fluconazole altered hyphal formation in ways that depended on susceptibility and concentration. Resistant isolates could retain hyphae. The tested between-drug difference was not statistically significant, and a change in fungal morphology does not establish reduced tissue invasion or improved symptoms in patients. Clinical inference is Low.

summary.text: An antifungal action and a Hedgehog pathway effect are separate observations. Itraconazole has cell and mouse evidence plus mixed human biomarker findings. Fluconazole and voriconazole had negative reporter findings in the cited experiments.
